rationale: C07 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the 1960 proclamation. Both use the same Flag Day authority and closely parallel operative sequence: call upon Federal, State, and local officials to arrange flag display on public buildings, then urge the public to fly the flag at homes or other suitable places and participate in commemorative ceremonies. C08 and C12 contain closely related annual formulations, but C07 most closely matches the later directive's combined wording and organization.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I call upon the responsible officers of the Federal Government and of the State and local governments to arrange for the flag to be flown on all public buildings on that day.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I ... call upon the appropriate officials of the Federal Government, and of the State and local Governments, to arrange for the display of our colors on all public buildings on Flag Day
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive near-verbatim administrative call directed to the same three levels of government for flag display on all public buildings.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I request the people of the United States to observe Flag Day by flying the colors at their homes and other suitable places, by organizing and participating in appropriate services and ceremonies
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I urge all of our people to observe the day by flying the Stars and Stripes at their homes or other suitable places and by participating in ceremonies especially designed to honor the flag
shared_material.explanation: The public-observance provision shares the same sequence and concrete means of observance: home display followed by participation in ceremonies.
